purpose: Reads a caller-declared business model as a closed set of boolean payment-activity facts and classifies it into the licence classes of one of three pinned payment-services regimes: Bermuda’s proposed Payment Services Act (consultation-response status: proposed, never presented as enacted), EU PSD2 Annex I with its Article 3 exclusions, and the UK Payment Services Regulations 2017 Schedule 1 Parts 1 and 2. Considers the regime’s exclusions against the declared facts (technical service providers, one-sided commercial agents, limited-network instruments), reports conflicts such as a declared technology-only model that holds customer funds, and emits transition notes (for example the transition note for existing Bermuda money service businesses). Refuses an unknown profile or a missing activities object with a recorded reason, and records non-boolean activity values as rejected inputs. The output is a structured reading of declared facts against pinned primary text, not legal advice: every payload carries not_legal_advice: true, and the page makes the same statement. Scope limits: no real firms or licence statuses, no threshold or perimeter arithmetic, no consumer-rights obligations (PSD2 Title III), and the Bermuda reading reflects proposed text only.
